title: Ecology federal permits record: West Sound Marina, Inc. Dredging (Aquatics 144990)

licence.text: Use allowed with credit and a link; commercial and political use prohibited

rows.label: What the project is
rows.value: Dredge up to 360 cubic yards of sediment in a shallow subtidal region next to an existing concrete pier within West Sound on Orcas Island, San Juan County, Washington. The proposed action is necessary to effectively remove chemical contamination, particularly TBT, in a shallow subtidal region that was impacted from boat maintenance and repair activities associated with the tidal grid and wood plank pier that were conducted prior to 1986. The remediation area is approximately 40 feet by 60 feet and extends north and south of both finger piers and underneath the main concrete pier. Sediment would be dredged using a diver-assisted hydraulic dredge. Based on results from previous sediment investigations, four feet of sediment would be removed from the remediation area. Dredged sediment would be pumped to a nearby barge fitted with Geotubes used to de-water the dredged sediment. The Geotubes would be inoculated with project-specific polymers to bind with suspended solids in the dredged material slurry, resulting in a clear effluent. Resulting water would be contained within the barge until it can be tested to ensure it meets standards established by the Department of Ecology. Once the effluent meets applicable standards, it would be discharged back into West Sound. Once dewatering is completed, the barge would be towed to the Waste Management transload facility on the Duwamish Waterway in Seattle. The Geotubes would be removed from the barge and loaded on either a truck or train for transport to a Subtitle D landfill. The purpose of the proposed action is to reduce the threat to human health and the environment by eliminating or substantially reducing one or more pathways for exposure to a hazardous
